slides.title: Expect bugs
slides.text: Programs break, and good programmers test on purpose. A test case is one board with a known right answer.
slides.alt: A Pro Debug Lab board with its test tabs above it: one program must pass every board, not just this one.

slides.title: One board can hide a bug
slides.text: A program can pass one board and fail another. Three test boards catch what one board misses.
slides.alt: The same program on a different test board: the board changed, the program did not, and a hidden bug can show here.

slides.title: Edge cases
slides.text: An edge case is an unusual input: a maze with no gems, a longer hallway, a goal right before a wall. It breaks assumptions you did not know you made.
slides.alt: A later Debug Lab board with an unusual layout: goals and walls sit where a program that assumes too much will fail.

slides.title: The debug loop
slides.text: The tabs above the board show a check mark or a cross for each test. A fix is done only when every tab passes.
slides.alt: The fixed Pro program under its test tabs: one program, three boards, and the fix counts only when all three pass.

words.means: one input with a known right answer
an unusual input that can break a program

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Robo Route at Debug Lab and fix 4 levels. After every change, run all the test boards again, and keep your edits few.
slides.alt: A Pro Debug Lab board with its test tabs above it: one program must pass every board, not just this one.
